cards.summary: AP reported that Tehran rejected Trump’s latest economic threats on Thursday while the wider Iran war continued to keep shipping, energy and humanitarian access unsettled.

cards.title: U.S. stocks recover as bond yields remain tense
cards.summary: AP reported the S&P 500 rose 0.4%, the Dow 1% and Nasdaq 0.4% Friday, while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.73%.
detail: Associated Press reported that U.S. stocks rose Friday: the S&P 500 gained 33.21 points to 7,674.37, the Dow rose 517.80 points to 53,277.01 and the Nasdaq added 113.29 points to 26,180.45.

The rebound came while the bond market stayed unsettled. AP reported the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.73% from 4.69% and Brent crude settled at $92.67, up 0.8%, keeping inflation and debt concerns in view.
This is a completed-session description, not a forecast. The next uncertainty is whether yields stabilize after the Treasury buyback intervention or continue to pressure risk assets.

cards.title: Fed minutes revive the possibility of higher rates
cards.summary: Minutes from the July meeting say many officials would likely support higher rates if inflation fails to decline, even as the September decision remains uncertain.
detail: The Federal Reserve released minutes from its July 28–29 meeting on Aug. 19. AP reported that many officials thought the central bank might need to lift its short-term rate in coming months if inflation did not subside; the committee had voted 9–3 to keep the rate near 3.6%.

The minutes identified inflation risks from the Iran war, tariffs and heavy AI-infrastructure investment. AP also reported that investors still expected the Fed to hold in September, while noting that market expectations could change.
The next evidence is incoming inflation, energy and labor data rather than a predetermined policy move. This card describes the policy signal and carries no investment recommendation.

cards.title: Asian shares are mixed as Treasury relief proves limited
cards.summary: AP reported Friday’s regional session was mostly higher: Kospi +0.9%, Hang Seng +1.1%, while Nikkei fell 0.3% as bond yields rose again.
detail: Associated Press reported that Asian shares were mostly higher on Friday, Aug. 21, after Wall Street’s retreat. The Kospi rose 0.9% to 6,912.95, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 1.1% to 25,967.58, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.3% to 66,016.36 and the Shanghai Composite was up less than 0.1% at 3,905.20.

AP said Treasury’s plan to at least double longer-term debt buybacks had only limited capacity to calm markets. U.S. 10-year yields were around 4.69%, and Asian bond yields also rose, keeping higher borrowing costs as the main cross-market driver.
Regional sessions close at different times, so this is a time-stamped regional reading rather than one completed Asia-wide close. The card is descriptive and does not recommend an investment action.
